title: Run the project locally
subtitle: Distinguish terminal, directory, runtime and dependencies.
concept: Follow project instructions with suitable tools in the correct directory. Read failures before choosing the next step.
intuition: A recipe's oven instruction assumes the right appliance, temperature and dish. Commands have prerequisites too.
objectives: Use a separate practice directory and check README and tool versions.
Keep errors and identify whether they occur during setup, installation or execution.

body.title: A terminal runs commands
body.text: Editors change files; terminals execute commands. Save appendix files by name in a separate practice directory and open it in your editor. Integrated terminals often start there; check the path. cd learning-list changes directory. Quote paths containing spaces. The wrong directory hides configuration and files.

body.title: Check tools before running
body.text: Install Git and Node.js using the official links for your system. Check git --version, node --version and npm --version. This example requires Node.js 22.12+ and defines npm test and npm start. Run tests, then start and open the printed local URL. Keep the terminal running; Ctrl+C stops the server.

body.title: Do not install blindly
body.text: Node projects with dependencies usually need packages installed. If README requires it and package-lock.json matches, npm ci recreates node_modules from the lockfile and fails on mismatch. This example needs no external packages. Keep errors and directory details; do not delete lockfiles, downgrade everything or run unfamiliar scripts without cause.

workedExamples.title: Run the example
workedExamples.problem: How do you start the study list?
steps: Save project files in learning-list and open a terminal there.
Check node --version, then run npm test.
Run npm start, open its URL and keep the terminal active.
workedExamples.answer: Expect passing tests and http://127.0.0.1:5180 in the terminal. Open that URL; Ctrl+C stops the server. No external packages means npm install is unnecessary here.

workedExamples.title: An occupied port
workedExamples.problem: Does EADDRINUSE mean upgrade every dependency?
steps: Record npm start and the full error.
The requested address or port is already in use.
Stop your own previous server, or explicitly change port and URL.
workedExamples.answer: Use Ctrl+C in your old terminal before restarting. Do not kill unknown processes. Changing port changes origin, so old localStorage records do not appear automatically.

commonMistakes.claim: Every project uses the same commands.
commonMistakes.correction: Commands come from project configuration and README; inspect first.

commonMistakes.claim: Deleting a lockfile is the simplest error fix.
commonMistakes.correction: It supports reproducible installation. Deletion changes dependency resolution; diagnose first.

practice.problem: package.json cannot be found. What first?
practice.hint: Where are the file and terminal?
practice.answer: Check whether the terminal is at the project root and configuration has the correct name and location.
solution: Do not install random packages in the wrong directory.

practice.answer: Follow official Node.js installation instructions or inspect PATH, reopen the terminal and check again.
solution: A missing tool is not a business-logic error.

practice.problem: npm ci fails because the lockfile does not match. What next?
practice.answer: Check branch, package.json and lockfile. Update consistently under repository conventions and review dependency changes; do not bypass by deleting the lockfile.
solution: Commit matching dependency files together when they change.

practice.problem: Why does the local URL stop working after closing the terminal?
practice.answer: The local server stopped. Restart it in the correct directory. Saved files and a running service are different states.
solution: Open the browser after startup succeeds.

learningCheck.question: What does EADDRINUSE directly mean?
choices: The requested listening address or port is occupied
feedback: It does not identify business-code failure.
This is a runtime-environment issue, separate from Git.
